question: Which hepatitis virus has the highest rate of progression to chronic infection following acute exposure in immunocompetent adults?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. HCV has the highest chronicity rate of all hepatitis viruses (70–85%). Its high mutation rate and quasispecies diversity allow immune evasion. The DAA revolution (sofosbuvir-based regimens) now achieves >95% sustained virological response in 12 weeks.

answers.text: Hepatitis B virus — chronicity rate of 5–10% in adults

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Adult HBV chronicity is only 5–10% (the mature immune system clears it in 90–95%). While neonatal HBV has 90% chronicity, overall HCV far exceeds HBV's rate in adult-acquired infection.

answers.text: Hepatitis E virus — high chronicity in endemic regions

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HEV is self-limiting in immunocompetent individuals with no chronicity. Rare chronic HEV (genotype 3) occurs only in immunosuppressed organ transplant recipients.

answers.text: Hepatitis A virus — persists as a carrier state in 30% of cases

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HAV never causes chronic infection or a carrier state. It is strictly self-limiting with complete recovery and lifelong immunity. There is no chronic HAV.

overallFeedback.feedback: Chronicity ranking: HCV (70–85%) >> HBV in neonates (90%) > HBV in adults (5–10%) > HAV and HEV (0% in immunocompetent). No vaccine exists for HCV.
HCV = highest chronicity (70–85%) → most likely to cause chronic liver disease → now curable with DAAs (sofosbuvir/ledipasvir, 12 weeks, >95% cure).
